speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of all countries, big and small, must be respected.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Foreign Minister.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first is to ask whether the Foreign Ministry was aware beforehand that the speech on 8 March was going to be delivered by the Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, the first question is whether the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) knew beforehand that the speech was being given and did MFA know the contents of the speech.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question is, earlier, Minister Shanmugam mentioned that Indivisible Security is perhaps a concept in International Relations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask the Foreign Minister what is the Government's view of such a principle of Indivisible Security.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And last of all, does the Foreign Minister agree that accepting a principle of Indivisible Security is very risky for small countries like Singapore?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Lim, I am not sure whether you are levelling all your supplementary questions to the Minister for Foreign Affairs or the Minister for Law?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Because I think your supplementaries actually cover some of what Minister Shanmugam earlier said.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: So, can I just be clear as to whom you are asking these questions?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Deputy Speaker, I am asking them to the Foreign Ministry because I would like to know the Government's view on this and the speech that was given covered foreign affairs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I believe that the views of MFA are very important.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We know generally when each Minister is going to speak, we are aware of that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I must tell you we do not personally check every single line and sentence in our speeches and the speeches can evolve according to the circumstances of the event.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Would the Foreign Minister agree that, actually, the Government's statements on Russia's invasion on Ukraine have been consistent all this while and there has never been this attempt to say that the US or NATO has been somewhat contributory to the current state of affairs, which was something that the Minister for Law did say?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like him to confirm that up to now, the Government has not taken this position and this is actually something new in the public domain.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our position has been and will continue to be clear and consistent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have said that on numerous occasions, not just in this House.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Various Ministers have also said this, in various fora outside this House.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I must add that foreign policy is something which we all have to take responsibility for, including the Opposition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, I think we must also be very clear in our minds that there are a diversity of views.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And when we are explaining these matters to the general public and to our population, or indeed, even in this House, it is not unreasonable to reflect the diversity of views.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But reflecting the diversity of views does not alter our national position, based on a defence of our national interests and the principles which a small, tiny city-state like us must subscribe to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, Mr Deputy Speaker, I detect, actually, unanimity in this House, across the partisan divide and I think we should maintain that discipline, that cohesion and that unity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier, the Minister said that there is collective responsibility in the Cabinet and that the Law Minister's views reflect the views of the Government.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In his speech, he actually said specifically that, in his view, the West and NATO were not uninvolved bystanders who had no role to play in the current situation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, do I take it that that is the Government's view as well?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Why have we taken such a categorical stand?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have taken it because of the vulnerabilities of Singapore as a tiny city-state.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And history is replete with tragedy and misfortune falling on small countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As the Minister for Law just explained – both in his speech and reiterated in this House – ultimately, the victim is the smaller country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you want to get into a larger debate on foreign policy, then, I would draw your attention to the fact that we are not in Europe.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As we collectively craft a foreign policy that is both consistent and protects our national interests, I would say that, on a larger strategic stage, we must always be aware.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, if you do not mind, let me recite what I said a year ago: "The events in Ukraine go to the heart of the fundamental norms of international law and the UN Charter that prohibit the use of force and acts of aggression against another sovereign state.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a clear and gross violation of the international norms, a completely unacceptable precedent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Ukraine is much smaller than Russia, but it is much bigger than Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And so, we cannot accept one country attacking another without justification, arguing that its independence was a result of historical errors or crazy decisions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Such a rationale would go against internationally recognised legitimacy and the territorial integrity of many countries, including Singapore." So, I think these are matters on which we are all agreed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You can get into the historical details of how a situation unfolded.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our objective in Southeast Asia is not to let a repeat of the European tragedy occur here, in this part of the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In trying to avoid a parallel of that situation here, I think it is entirely legitimate for us to consider all views, diverse views, opposing views even, on how the situation in Europe came about.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would urge the Member to understand what is at state, understand why we have taken a stand, understand why that stand has to be maintained, upheld and, I hope, shared across the House by all the parties represented here; and also agree that we must not let a repeat of Europe – a continent which unfortunately has been a source of two world wars in the last century – we do not want a repeat of that here.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And finally, remember that a small nation is always vulnerable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And again, to repeat something I have said multiple times here, never let ourselves be a vassal state, a stalking horse, a cat's paw for any other power.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Understand that when we get entangled in such matters, the ultimate loser is always the smaller state.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Lim, you have asked four or five supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I invite you to ask your final one.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Based on the Minister's last answer, he did not say whether the Government agreed with the Law Minister's view that the West and NATO were not uninvolved bystanders who had no role to play in the current situation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, do I take it from him that he would rather not go into such historical matters?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are things that we – when we are having a forum in Parliament and with the general public, when there is a need to reflect the diversity of views.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I think it was entirely legitimate for the Minister for Law to do so.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, as the Minister for Foreign Affairs, my first job is to protect the sovereignty, the independence and the territorial integrity of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I say it my way, but I believe that my statements are entirely consistent with the rest of my Cabinet colleagues, and we stand and we take collective responsibility for that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think I have said enough, Mr Deputy Speaker, and I am still absolutely certain that there is unanimity in this House on this matter of the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I thank the Member for her support.
